newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK BoE inflation report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK BoE inflation report.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to the Bank of England's November inflation report published at 1130 GMT.
The Bank said a further interest rate rise was likely to be needed in due course and added there was now much less chance of inflation below 2.5 percent in 1997.
"The surprise is that the Bank are being more aggressive than expected. The Bank is tightening the screws."
PETER LUXTON, ECONOMIC ADVISER, MMS INTERNATIONAL

"The Bank didn't like the last rate cut so in a sense the latest rise simply undoes the damage done earlier in the year. We're still seeing strong numbers coming out -- above trend growth, the recovery broadening and strengthening, house prices picking up. They must be worried that the Chancellor is going to get behind in the game all the time. Things might look good at the moment but they may not stay very good for very long."
ADRIAN OWENS, ECONOMIST AT JULIUS BAER

"It's a disappointing report. The Bank is wary of a near term increase in inflation, in contrast with the last report when they were expecting near-term falls. The Bank is implying that higher interest rates are needed, and is downplaying the effects of an 8.5 percent rise in sterling."
KEVIN ADAMS, GILTS ANALYST AT BZW

"The thing that sticks out is the Bank's comments about sterling, that the rise will be temporary. I think they are being a bit pessimistic and not giving enough credit to the sterling situation. If British monetary policy appears prudent, the currency will hold up."
